motions.topic: Fuse a lexical-overlap gate with the packed cosine in the retrieval answer path: surface a hit as 'the answer' only when (a) its packed cosine exceeds a calibrated threshold, OR (b) the query's content terms literally appear in the document key/text (filename terms, not the opaque fragment index). Otherwise report 'no confident match' and fall through to the co-processor verdict — never a merely-similar document for a query whose terms appear nowhere. MEASURED (live, this host): /k3/retrieve packed cosine scores are compressed into 0.17-0.40; real matches and noise overlap — 'turbovec'->0.373 (task_card, real), 'monad'->0.20 (paper_18_monad_philosophy.md, real), 'voltage doctrine'->0.245 (task_card, real), vs 'capabilities'->0.25 (enwikiquote fragment, no match), 'engines'->0.24 (fragment, no match), 'zxqwpvy nonsense'->0.176 (random task_card, no match). A fixed threshold cannot separate the 0.20 real 'monad' from the 0.176 noise. The chat answer path currently surfaces ANY readable hit as 'the answer' regardless of score, so gibberish returns a random document at cosine ~0.18 (observed after the fragment fix). REJECT AS PREMATURE if the document keys are opaque (hash-only, no readable filename terms), in which case the lexical signal is unreliable and the honest fallback is to label every surfaced doc with its score and 'low-confidence' instead of claiming a match.
